setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1. Nothing has been edited yet, so the channel's memory (its list of remembered edits) is empty.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 down to History and press K3. The Memory screen shows your position in the channel's remembered edits, as 'position of total'. It reads 0 of 0 because nothing has been edited yet.
steps.title: Open History

steps.caption: With nothing remembered, K2, K3 and E3 in History do nothing: the counter stays at 0 of 0. Tap Play (1,8): channel 1 plays C D E F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear the original phrase

steps.caption: Open Masks (E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). Any MIDI keyboard or controller connected to the norns can write onto a held step: hold step 1 and play note 72 at velocity 90, release, then hold step 2 and play note 76 at velocity 80. Each is one edit that Memory keeps. Reopen History: the counter reads 2 of 2, meaning you are at edit 2 of the 2 remembered.
steps.title: Record two step edits

steps.caption: Tap Play: the phrase is 72, 76, 64, 65 at velocities 90, 80, 107, 97, because steps 1 and 2 carry your edits. Now, in History, turn E3 one detent left. The counter reads 1 of 2: the second edit is undone.
steps.title: Undo the second edit

steps.caption: Tap Play: step 1 keeps your recorded note 72 at velocity 90, and step 2 is back to its original note 62 at velocity 117.
steps.title: Hear the undone state

steps.caption: Turn E3 left again: the counter reads 0 of 2, the oldest state, before either edit. (K2 jumps straight here.)
steps.title: Return to the first state

steps.caption: Tap Play: the original four-step phrase 60, 62, 64, 65 is back. Then turn E3 left three more times. The counter stays at 0 of 2: you cannot go further back than the first state.
steps.title: Stop at the oldest state

steps.caption: Tap Play: still the original phrase. Then turn E3 right once. The counter reads 1 of 2: step 1 has its edit back.
steps.title: Redo the first edit

steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 64, 65, so only the first edit is back. Then turn E3 right once more. The counter is back at 2 of 2.
steps.title: Redo both edits

steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 76, 64, 65, both recorded edits are back.
steps.title: Hear both edits again

steps.caption: Turn E3 right three times: the counter stays at 2 of 2, the newest state. Tap Play for 72, 76, 64, 65, press K2 to jump all the way back (0 of 2, the original phrase when you play), then press K3 to jump forward to 2 of 2 (both edits again). Now turn E3 left once: the counter reads 1 of 2 and the second edit is undone, so a new edit will replace it.
steps.title: Undo one step again

steps.caption: Open Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 79 at velocity 70, release, then reopen History. The counter reads 2 of 2 again, but it is a different second action: the new edit replaced the undone one.
steps.title: Replace the undone action

steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 79, 65. Step 1 keeps its edit, step 2 is back to its original 62 and step 3 plays your new note 79. The old second edit (76) is gone.
steps.title: Hear the new branch

title: Undo, redo and replace a remembered edit
